summary: The Toaster page documents the component that renders all toasts and can be placed anywhere in the app. It explains that toasts expand on hover, that expand makes that the default, and that visibleToasts changes how many are shown (default 3). It covers the six positions, multiple toasters routed with id and toasterId, and spacing from the screen edge: offset defaults to 32px on desktop and mobileOffset to 16px below a 600px screen width. It also shows how to make the toaster follow the app's light or dark theme through next-themes. The API table lists the container defaults: theme light, richColors false, expand false, visibleToasts 3, position bottom-right, closeButton false, gap 14, dir ltr and hotkey ⌥/alt + T.
key_ideas: Toaster renders every toast and can be placed anywhere in the app.
Hovering one toast expands the pile; expand makes the expanded state the default.
Three toasts are visible by default; visibleToasts changes that number.
Six positions are available, and bottom-right is the default.
Several toasters can coexist when you need a clear separation; each has an id and toasts pick one with toasterId.
Toasts sit 32px from the screen edge on desktop and 16px on mobile by default.
mobileOffset applies when the screen is narrower than 600px.
offset and mobileOffset accept a number, a string such as 10vh, or an object of individual sides.
The toaster's theme defaults to light; pass the resolved app theme (for example from next-themes) to follow dark mode.
Swipe directions are derived from the position unless swipeDirections is set.
Other container defaults: gap 14, dir ltr, hotkey ⌥/alt + T, richColors false, closeButton false, invert false.

rules.rule: Render the <Toaster /> component to display toasts; it can be placed anywhere in the app.
rules.why: This component renders all the toasts.
rules.evidence: This component renders all the toasts, you can place it anywhere in your app.

rules.rule: Toasts expand when the user hovers one of them; set the expand prop to true to make the expanded state the default (expand is false by default).
rules.why: When you hover on one of the toasts they expand, and setting expand to true makes that the default behaviour; the API table lists expand as false by default.
rules.evidence: You can make that the default behavior by setting the expand prop to true

rules.rule: Visible toasts default to 3; change the count with the visibleToasts prop (the example uses 9).
rules.why: The default number of visible toasts is 3; visibleToasts customizes it.
rules.evidence: 9 toasts will be visible instead of the default, which is 3.

rules.rule: Place toasts with the position prop, choosing top-left, top-center, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-center or bottom-right; the default is bottom-right.
rules.why: Position changes where all toasts are rendered; the API table lists bottom-right as the default.
rules.evidence: Changes the place where all toasts will be rendered.

rules.rule: Render more than one Toaster only when you need a clear separation; give each an id and send each toast to one with toasterId.
rules.why: Multiple toasters are for when you need this clear separation, and they let you point a toast to a specific toaster.

rules.rule: Offsets default to 32px on desktop and 16px on mobile; change them with the offset and mobileOffset props.
rules.why: The docs give a default desktop offset of 32px and a default mobile offset of 16px, both customizable through offset and mobileOffset.
rules.evidence: Default desktop offset is 32px and default mobile offset is 16px

rules.rule: Set mobile spacing with mobileOffset, which applies when the screen width is less than 600px.
rules.why: mobileOffset is applied below a 600px screen width.
rules.evidence: mobileOffset will be applied when the screen width is less than 600px

rules.rule: Give offset a number for the same spacing on all sides, a string such as "10vh" for relative units, or an object to set individual sides.
rules.why: The page shows all three forms of offset.

rules.rule: To change only some mobile sides, pass mobileOffset an object with just those sides; the rest keep their default values.
rules.why: The example sets only bottom and says the rest use default values.
rules.evidence: mobile offset will be 16px from the bottom, default values for the rest

rules.rule: Make the toaster follow the app's theme by wrapping it in a 'use client' component that passes the theme provider's resolvedTheme (for example from next-themes) to the theme prop.
rules.why: This makes the toaster's theme adapt to the app's theme; theme otherwise defaults to light, so dark-mode apps would show light toasts. [inferred]

rules.rule: Let swipe directions follow the toaster's position (the default), and set swipeDirections only to override them.
rules.why: The API table lists swipeDirections with a default that is based on position.

rules.rule: Turn on richColors on the Toaster when typed toasts should use rich colors; it is false by default.
rules.why: The API table lists richColors as a boolean defaulting to false.

rules.rule: Turn on closeButton on the Toaster to show close buttons; it is false by default.
rules.why: The API table lists closeButton as a boolean defaulting to false.

rules.rule: Set the dir prop for right-to-left interfaces; it defaults to ltr. [inferred]
rules.why: The API table lists dir as a string defaulting to ltr.

rules.rule: Set the toaster's keyboard shortcut with the hotkey prop; the default is ⌥/alt + T.
rules.why: The API table lists hotkey with the default ⌥/alt + T.

rules.rule: Space the toasts with the gap prop, which defaults to 14. [inferred]
rules.why: The API table lists gap as a number defaulting to 14; the page does not describe what it spaces or its unit.

rules.rule: Set shared per-toast defaults through toastOptions and default icons through icons on the Toaster.
rules.why: The API table lists toastOptions and icons as Toaster props.

rules.rule: Leave invert at its default of false unless toasts should be inverted.
rules.why: The API table lists invert as a boolean defaulting to false; the page does not describe the inverted look.

options.effect: The toasts expand when the user hovers one of them.

options.name: Always expanded
options.effect: The expanded state becomes the default; combine with visibleToasts to show more than 3.
options.when: When every visible toast should be expanded without hovering.

decisions.question: Where should the toaster sit on screen?

options.name: top-left
options.effect: All toasts render at the top left.

options.name: top-right

options.name: bottom-left
options.effect: All toasts render at the bottom left.
options.when: When the layout calls for it; the multiple-toasters example puts its 'canvas' toaster here.

options.name: bottom-center
options.effect: All toasts render centred at the bottom.
options.when: When the layout calls for it.

options.name: bottom-right
options.effect: All toasts render at the bottom right.

decisions.question: One toaster for the whole app, or several?

options.name: One toaster
options.effect: All toasts appear in a single place.
options.when: When no separation between kinds of toasts is needed. [inferred]

options.name: Multiple toasters
options.effect: Each Toaster has an id and position, and toasts are routed with toasterId, for example a 'global' toaster top-right and a 'canvas' toaster bottom-left.
options.when: When you need this clear separation.

decisions.recommendation: Render multiple toasters only if you need the clear separation.

decisions.question: Should toasts use a fixed theme or follow the app's theme?

options.name: Fixed light (default)
options.effect: The toaster uses the light theme regardless of the app.
options.when: Default when no theme prop is passed.

options.name: Follow the app theme
options.effect: The toaster adapts to the app's theme using the resolved theme from a provider such as next-themes.
options.when: When the app has a theme provider.

decisions.question: Should toasts show a close button?

options.name: No close button (default)
options.effect: Toasts render without a close button; closeButton is false.
options.when: Default when closeButton is not set.

options.name: Close button
options.effect: Every toast from this Toaster shows a close button.
options.when: Set closeButton on the Toaster; clicking it fires onDismiss (Other page). [inferred]

process.detail: Render <Toaster /> anywhere in the app; it renders all toasts.
Choose a position, and adjust offset (default 32px) and mobileOffset (default 16px, applied below 600px) as a number, a string or a per-side object if the defaults do not fit.
Create a 'use client' Toaster wrapper that reads resolvedTheme from useTheme() (next-themes) and passes it to Sonner's Toaster as theme={resolvedTheme as ToasterProps['theme']}.
Render additional <Toaster id="..." position="..." /> instances and pass toasterId in toast() options to route each toast.

examples.visual_note: A 'global' toaster top-right and a 'canvas' toaster bottom-left, with buttons that send toasts to each through toasterId.
offset={16} (16px on all sides), offset="10vh" (10vh on all sides), a per-side object of 24px bottom and 16px right and left, and mobileOffset={{ bottom: '16px' }}.
A client component that imports Toaster as SonnerToaster and ToasterProps from 'sonner', and useTheme from 'next-themes', then passes resolvedTheme to the theme prop.
<Toaster expand visibleToasts={9} /> shows 9 toasts instead of the default 3.

caveats: The API table lists toastOptions with a default of 4000, which looks like a documentation slip, since toastOptions is an object and 4000 is the toast duration default. [inferred]
